parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **economic growth**?
choices: The pattern of rises and falls in real GDP over time around the long-term trend rate of growth
GDP adjusted for inflation so it measures changes in the volume of output
An increase in the output of goods and services in an economy over time, measured by the change in real GDP
The value of all the final output made inside a country's borders over a period of time, usually one year

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (An increase in the output of goods and services in an economy over time, measured by the change in real GDP)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of economic cycle
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of real GDP
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of gross domestic product (GDP)

parts.text:
In 2019, Novaris experienced rapid economic growth of 7.1%, while inflation rose to 6.0%.

Explain why faster economic growth might be accompanied by rising prices.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

Example:
- Rapid growth increases total demand (1) and if supply cannot keep up, firms raise prices (1), so demand-pull inflation rises, as shown by inflation of 6.0% when growth reached 7.1% (1)
rows.notes: Accept any other valid explanation. Answers with no reference to the context cannot gain the third mark.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **inflation**?
choices: Income adjusted for inflation showing the quantity of goods and services it can buy
A sustained rise in the general price level over a period of time
The costs to firms of changing prices such as reprinting price lists and updating websites
A sustained fall in the general price level over a period of time

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (A sustained rise in the general price level over a period of time)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of real income
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of menu costs
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of deflation

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **deflation**?

A sustained fall in the general price level over a period of time

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **balance of payments**?
choices: The part of the balance of payments that records trade in goods and services plus primary and secondary income flows
When the value of money flowing in on the current account is greater than the money flowing out
Goods and services bought from other countries
A record of all financial transactions between one country and the rest of the world

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (A record of all financial transactions between one country and the rest of the world)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account surplus
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of imports

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **current account**?
choices: Goods and services bought from other countries
The part of the balance of payments that records trade in goods and services plus primary and secondary income flows
When the value of money flowing in on the current account is greater than the money flowing out
Goods and services sold to other countries

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The part of the balance of payments that records trade in goods and services plus primary and secondary income flows)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of imports
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of current account surplus
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of exports

rows.answer:

A: incorrect, that is the meaning of imports
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of balance of payments
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of trade in services

parts.text: Define the term **balance of payments**.

parts.text: Define the term **current account deficit**.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **redistribution of income**?
choices: A tax where the same percentage of income is paid whatever the level of income
When people do not have enough income to meet basic needs such as food, shelter and clothing
A tax where the percentage of income paid rises as income rises
The transfer of income from some groups to others usually from richer to poorer households through taxes and benefits

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (The transfer of income from some groups to others usually from richer to poorer households through taxes and benefits)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of proportional tax
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of absolute poverty
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of progressive tax

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **sustainability**?
choices: A resource that can be replaced naturally such as wind, solar energy or managed forests
A resource that will run out because it cannot be replaced, such as oil or coal
Meeting the needs of the present without reducing the ability of future generations to meet their needs
The release of harmful substances or noise into the environment which damages health and ecosystems

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (Meeting the needs of the present without reducing the ability of future generations to meet their needs)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of renewable resource
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of non-renewable resource
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of pollution

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **fiscal policy**?
choices: When government spending is greater than government revenue in a year
Increasing government spending and/or cutting taxes to increase total demand

A tax on income or wealth paid directly to the government, such as income tax

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **monetary policy**?
choices: When the central bank creates new money to buy financial assets and increase the money supply
The cost of borrowing money and the reward for saving

The use of interest rates and the money supply by the central bank to influence the economy

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **supply-side policies**?
choices: Changes to labour laws and benefits to make the labour market more flexible
The ability of workers to move between jobs or between areas
Government policies that aim to increase the productive capacity of the economy, for example by improving the quality of labour
The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (Government policies that aim to increase the productive capacity of the economy, for example by improving the quality of labour)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour market reform
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour mobility
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of infrastructure

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **infrastructure**?
choices: Changes to labour laws and benefits to make the labour market more flexible
The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband
The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition
Government policies that aim to increase the productive capacity of the economy, for example by improving the quality of labour

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour market reform
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of deregulation
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of supply-side policies

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **deregulation**?
choices: The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband
The ability of workers to move between jobs or between areas
The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition
Changes to labour laws and benefits to make the labour market more flexible

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of infrastructure
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour mobility
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour market reform

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **labour market reform**?
choices: The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition
The basic physical systems a country needs to function such as roads, railways, ports and broadband

The ability of workers to move between jobs or between areas

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (Changes to labour laws and benefits to make the labour market more flexible)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of deregulation
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of infrastructure
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour mobility

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **tax incentives**?
choices: Reductions in taxes designed to encourage firms to invest or people to work
The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition
Government policies that aim to increase the productive capacity of the economy, for example by improving the quality of labour
The ability of workers to move between jobs or between areas

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (Reductions in taxes designed to encourage firms to invest or people to work)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of deregulation
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of supply-side policies
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour mobility

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **labour mobility**?
choices: The ability of workers to move between jobs or between areas

The removal of government rules and controls to increase competition

rows.answer:

B: incorrect, that is the meaning of labour market reform
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of infrastructure
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of deregulation

parts.text: The main aim of supply-side policies is to

increase the budget deficit
increase the productive capacity of the economy
increase interest rates

A: incorrect
B: incorrect
D: incorrect

parts.text: A disadvantage of supply-side policies is that
choices: they reduce productivity
they reduce the PPC
they take a long time to have an effect
they always cause inflation

A: incorrect
B: incorrect
D: incorrect

parts.text: Which one of the following is most likely to shift a country's PPC outwards?

Better education and training
A rise in unemployment

A: incorrect

parts.text: Cutting the rate of income tax is a supply-side policy because it
choices: raises government revenue immediately
increases the price of imports
reduces the labour force
increases the incentive for people to work

A: incorrect, lower tax rates usually reduce revenue in the short run
B: incorrect, income tax does not change import prices
C: incorrect, it is intended to have the opposite effect

parts.text: Which one of the following supply-side policies is most likely to reduce structural unemployment?

Retraining schemes for workers in declining industries
An increase in pensions
A cut in interest rates

A: incorrect

D: incorrect

parts.text: Deregulation of an industry is most likely to

increase the number of rules firms must follow
nationalise the industry
raise barriers to entry

B: incorrect
C: incorrect
D: incorrect
